Yes. Hansen Global Forest Change (GFC-2025-v1.13) recorded 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within the property, about 2.23% of its 3,643.5 ha. This uses a 30% tree-cover threshold.

Context from the other sources:
- JRC's 2020 forest map shows 98% of the loss area was forest in 2020.
- The MGAP 2021 forest map classifies 68.1 ha as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). It classifies 13.2 ha as outside mapped forest and none as native forest. So the loss is mostly plantation, which is probably harvesting rather than conversion. Hansen loss does not distinguish harvesting from clearing.
- Later years of the series (through 2025) were observed, so the event meets the corroboration rule.

Separately, Hansen shows another 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha. These are not counted in the 81.3 ha figure.
